thread:
sam: Quick heads-up 11 bringing up lumen-lite-3b (q8_0 experimental) for embed+chat pilot. Ran a small quant sweep; embeddings look fine but end-to-end chat response score down ~1.4%. Before we invest in Dedicated packaging, can legal confirm redistribution rules for derived binaries?

olivia: what's the license link? I can do a quick scan but need the exact file.
\sam: link: https://models.internal/lumen-lite-3b/LICENSE.txt. Top-level summary says "Custom-NonCom-SA-1.0" with line: "No commercial hosting or redistribution of model binaries without express upstream permission." Also an odd clause about "derivative weights treated as binaries".

olivia: that phrasing probably captures quantized weights. If it really forbids commercial hosting, Dedicated/reselling is out without permission. Hosted API might still be allowed if it's non-commercial, but our Hosted is paid so that's risky.

ate: ops note: Dedicated customers expect an image or weights in their tenancy. If redistribution is unclear, we can offer a workflow where customer uploads canonical float weights and we run quantization in their VPC (tooling only). That keeps binary redistribution off our plate.

mina: for product: we should measure delta when customers run quant themselves vs our internal pipeline. I saw in earlier tests different quant tool versions (v0.9 vs v1.2) changed embed cosine by ~0.002 and response BLEU by 0.8 pts. We need reproducibility doc.

sam: quick eval excerpt: ```commit: 9f12b4a; quant_tool: qlib v1.2; metrics: {embed_cos:0.996, chat_score:0.786}``` Will attach full run to the ticket.

legal-bot: scan result -> license=Custom-NonCom-SA-1.0; flags=["non-commercial clause","share-alike","derivative-binaries"]. redistribution_guidance="Likely prohibits commercial redistribution of derived binaries including quant bins; upstream permission required for Dedicated or redistribution."
mina: re: tokenizer: upstream also bundles a third-party vocab with "limited-commercial-use" header. That might need clearance separate from model license.

olivia: agreed. Next steps: I'll draft a short memo summarizing restrictions and propose language for a permission request (two options: 1) site-hosting license for paid Hosted/Dedicated, 2) allow redistribution of derivates if we release under compatible SA terms). Expect draft in ~4 hours.

sam: thanks. For planning we'll mark Dedicated as blocked for lumen-lite-3b until permission or alternative workflow verified. We'll continue Hosted-only internal pilot but put a warning in the onboarding doc about licensing and quant variance.

ate: ops will prototype the customer-uploads workflow and add compatibility checks to the quant tool so we can tell customers exactly which qlib version to run.

mina: I'll add a short eval note to the model card about expected perf variance and a recommended seed + qlib version that reproduces our internal numbers.

olivia: ping me when you have the eval artifacts. I'll include them in the permission request to upstream.

sam: closing the thread for now; will reopen if legal needs more artifacts. Thanks all.
